unit.title: Describing Things in the Right Order

grammar_concept.title: Adjective Order
grammar_concept.rule: When more than one adjective comes before a noun, they follow a fixed order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material, purpose, then the noun. ("a beautiful small old round French wooden dining table")
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Native speakers follow this order automatically, without thinking about it — but it's genuinely fixed, not flexible like it is in Portuguese. Getting it wrong doesn't usually block understanding, but it sounds noticeably foreign.
grammar_concept.example: She bought a beautiful old French chair. (opinion → age → origin, never any other order)
grammar_concept.example_translation: Ela comprou uma bela cadeira francesa antiga.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português, os adjetivos costumam vir DEPOIS do substantivo, numa ordem bastante livre ("uma cadeira francesa antiga e bonita", "uma cadeira bonita e antiga francesa" — várias ordens soam aceitáveis). Isso leva a colocar vários adjetivos em inglês numa ordem aleatória antes do substantivo ("a French old beautiful chair"), o que soa claramente estranho a um falante nativo, mesmo sendo perfeitamente compreensível.
grammar_concept.correction: Antes de um substantivo, coloque os adjetivos por esta ordem: opinião (beautiful, nice) → tamanho (small, big) → idade (old, new) → forma (round, square) → cor (red, blue) → origem (French, Chinese) → material (wooden, plastic) → finalidade (dining, sleeping) → substantivo.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Describing an item for sale online: "Selling a lovely small antique round wooden coffee table."

vocabulary.definition_en: very pleasant or attractive (an opinion adjective)
very old and often valuable (an age adjective)
example_sentences: They bought an antique wooden clock.

vocabulary.definition_en: shaped like a rectangle (a shape adjective)
example_sentences: We need a large rectangular rug for the living room.

correct_answer: She bought a beautiful old French chair.
distractors: She bought a French old beautiful chair.
She bought an old French beautiful chair.
She bought a French beautiful old chair.
exercises.explanation: A ordem correta é opinião (beautiful) → idade (old) → origem (French) → substantivo.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Colocar a origem ("French") antes da opinião ou da idade é um erro muito comum, por o português não ter uma ordem tão rígida.

correct_answer: We bought a lovely small round wooden table.
distractors: We bought a wooden small round lovely table.
We bought a round wooden small lovely table.
We bought a small lovely wooden round table.
exercises.explanation: A ordem correta é opinião (lovely) → tamanho (small) → forma (round) → material (wooden) → substantivo.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Colocar o material ("wooden") logo no início é um erro comum, quando devia vir quase no fim, mesmo antes do substantivo.

exercises.prompt: Which word describes something very old and often valuable, like a piece of furniture?
exercises.explanation: "Antique" descreve objetos antigos e frequentemente valiosos, tipicamente móveis ou objetos de decoração.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What is the speaker describing?
correct_answer: a lovely small antique round wooden coffee table
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I'm selling a lovely small antique round wooden coffee table."
exercises.transcript: I'm selling a lovely small antique round wooden coffee table — it's in great condition and would look perfect in a cosy living room.

exercises.prompt: Read: "The shop window displayed a stunning large red Italian leather handbag, priced at 200 euros." Where was the handbag made?
exercises.explanation: "Italian" no texto indica a origem do produto: feito em Itália.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Comprei uma bonita mesa redonda de madeira."
correct_answer: I bought a beautiful round wooden table.
I bought a lovely round wooden table.
exercises.explanation: A ordem em inglês é opinião (beautiful/lovely) → forma (round) → material (wooden) → substantivo — diferente da ordem livre em português.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir palavra a palavra na ordem do português ("a wooden round beautiful table") é o erro mais comum aqui.

lesson.title: Describing Things in the Right Order

steps.content: When several adjectives are listed before a noun, each one usually gets a light rising intonation, with the whole list flowing quickly — native speakers don't pause between each adjective the way beginners often do.

steps.prompt: Describe an object near you (or one you own) using at least 2 adjectives in the correct order — try opinion + material, or size + colour.
Write 3 sentences, each describing an object using 2-3 adjectives in the correct order (opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, material).
